short_answer: Four distinct memory architectures have emerged: flat vector stores (Mem0, Zep), episodic page-in/page-out systems (Letta, MemGPT), knowledge-graph-backed stores (GraphRAG on Neo4j or TypeDB), and hybrid combinations. Vector databases retrieve semantically similar content via embedding search: fast, zero cold-start, and excellent for unstructured recall. Knowledge graphs traverse explicit entity relationships: deterministic, multi-hop, and explainable. Episodic systems use a context-resident working memory with long-term records in an external vector or structured store, but suffer from attentional dilution within the context window. Hybrid AI agents blend LLM generative responses with knowledge-graph-backed curated knowledge, enabling human-governed delivery alongside real-time generation.
